On Wed, 4 Mar 2015, Vaclav Petras wrote:

> Hi,
>
> can somebody summarize for me what is the status of spgrass*/rgrass*
> packages? I remember that the package for 7 should be `rgrass7` but now I
> see `spgrass` for G7 in the `spgrass` project description but I guess it is
> just a typo because R packages page says `rgrass7`. So just the project is
> `spgrass`? Then there is also the package which will use Rcpp and GRASS GIS
> C library, right?

Right with regard to the choice of rgrass7 as the name of the forthcoming 
package, currently I'm waiting for the PROJ 4.9.1 release before 
installing GRASS 7.0 locally before releasing. For the source package and 
the Windows binary, installation from R-Forge is by:

install.packages("rgrass7", repos="http://R-Forge.R-project.org")

OSX users would have to install from source until a CRAN submission is 
made (after R 3.1.3 is released shortly, but before R 3.2.0 in April).

I do not believe that an R package linking to the libgis library has any 
merit. It would be almost impossible to support cross-platform, and would 
offer very little that isn't already available.

Roger

Thanks,

Ben Holland

messages.subject: [GRASS-stats] v.isochrones in spgrass7
messages.body_plain:
On Sun, 15 Mar 2015, yogeshbansal wrote:

> Hi everyone,
>
> I am able to use the v.isochrones addon in GRASS7. But if i try to use the
> v.isochrones command by wrapping it in execGRASS() it says the
> v.iochrones.exe doesn't exist. I checked the issue and what i could
> understand is the v.isochrones addon is run directly using it's python
> scritp and a .exe file for same is not stored when i install this addon.
>
> So is there any way i can use the v.isochrones from inside R using spgrass7
> package?

Yes, use system() or system2() as this should "see" the same things as 
GRASS "sees".

I have no access to a Windows system running GRASS 7 with extensions and 
rgrass7. You can try running parseGRASS() yourself under debug() to see 
what happens when pyScripts is read. Or look at:

get("pyScripts", envir=rgrass7:::.GRASS_CACHE)

in Windows to see which values are present. As rgrass7 loads, the files in

basename(list.files(paste(Sys.getenv("WINGISBASE"),
       "scripts", sep="/"), pattern="py$"))

should be placed in this character vector, removing the file extension.

If they are not in this list and are not in the exclusion list, the 
assumption is that they are regular *.exe modules.

What we do not know, is whether addons are handled properly. I cannot 
check this, so need input from users who can check it.

Roger

messages.subject: [GRASS-stats] Error rgrass7 using readRAST()
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am testing rgrass7 and trying to read a single raster file calling R 
from GRASS. I am using the function readRAST(). Currently, this return a 
SpatialGridDataFrame R object but it seems to have a bug when reading 
the correct number of observations. In my case the input raster is 100 x 
100 so it should have 10,000 observations (ncell). Instead, readRAST() 
read 100 x 101 with 10,100 observations. Did anybody encounter this 
issue or know what it could be caused by?
I can send over my input raster if that helps to test on your machines.

Any help is much appreciated.

Thank you.
Francesco

messages.subject: [GRASS-stats] Error rgrass7 using readRAST()
messages.body_plain:
Roger,

Apparently the error was due to a mismatch with the default g.region. 
After checking in GRASS for g.region -p I found that it was set to 100 x 
101 columns. If any of you ever encounter the same problem, just make 
sure to set the g.region using the same input raster of interest, i.e. 
using g.region raster=/your_raster_name/.

Are there any plans to make use of the 'raster' package so that 
readRAST() reads a 'raster' R obj instead of a sp griddataframe? Same 
for writeRAST().

Thank you,
Francesco
